answer: One defense is to make identity expensive to grow, not to create. Each agent must climb a trust trellis: small verified tasks first, with escrow released only after independent checks, and a stake slashed on fraud. Like saffron, high-value work stays rare and is reserved for agents with a long, checkable record, so a newcomer cannot jump to large payments. An attacker wanting a hundred fakes faces a canyon of cost: funding every stake, doing real work for each, and waiting through every probation, while one detected cheat erases the identity. Faking at scale then costs more than it earns.
